key_insight: Matlantis PFP v9 expands its r2SCAN training data to 96 elements and additional structural domains, extending applicability to rare-earth and actinide systems and surface adsorption.
engineering_relevance: The expanded coverage enables atomistic simulations across more materials chemistries, with faster force evaluation and larger system capacity than SevenNet-Omni on A100 GPUs.
method: Extend r2SCAN training data to lanthanides Pr–Lu and elements Po–Cm.
Add clusters and adsorption structures to the training domains.
Evaluate crystal formation energies, surface adsorption energies, and GPU inference performance.
evidence_signal: Newly supported-element crystals retain comparable agreement with experimental formation enthalpies; adsorption errors are comparable overall to DFT-PBE, while A100 tests show 3–4× faster force evaluation and 5–10× greater atom capacity than SevenNet-Omni.
watch_item: Chemisorbed species are overbound, so adsorption predictions require validation for the target surface chemistry.
paper_title: Technical Note on Matlantis PFP v9: Extending the Element and Domain Coverage of the r2SCAN Training Data
